title: Avoid replaying historical local-refusal notices after host restart
outcome: Restart recovery preserves a local-refusal notice that has not yet been presented without repeatedly resurfacing historical notices already presented to the requester.
acceptance: After a local refusal has been presented to its owning session, normal host restart does not requeue the same historical notice; completion is associated with the exact original registration.

An interruption before first presentation still recovers a bounded readable refusal. Existing ownership, privacy, no producer send/credit, compaction and mirror repair remain unchanged; a queued-but-lost in-memory line is not falsely treated as delivered.

Behavioral tests distinguish before-presentation and after-presentation restarts, repeated restarts and newer notices, and the exact landing input passes the required full gate and independent review pair.
